title: The 1994 Italian general election is won by Silvio Berlusconi
text: The 1994 Italian general election was held on 27 and 28 March 1994 to elect members of the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate of the Republic for the 12th legislature. Silvio Berlusconi's centre-right coalition won a large majority in the Chamber of Deputies but just missed winning a majority in the Senate.

title: Murder of Antonella Di Veroli
text: On 10 April 1994, 47-year-old Antonella Di Veroli was killed in her home in Rome, Italy. The crime is unsolved as of 2026.

title: The 20th G7 summit was held in Naples.
text: The 20th G7 Summit was held in Naples, Italy, on 8–10 July 1994. The venue for the summit meetings was the former Royal Palace in Naples.

title: Brazil wins the FIFA World Cup by defeating Italy, 3–2, following a penalty shootout in the final game at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, California, USA.
text: The Rose Bowl is an outdoor athletic stadium located in Pasadena, California, United States. Opened in October 1922, the stadium is recognized as a National Historic Landmark and a California Historic Civil Engineering landmark.

title: The 1994 Italian Grand Prix, originally scheduled for 12 August, is held at Monza and won by Damon Hill.
text: The 1994 Italian Grand Prix was a Formula One motor race held on 11 September 1994 at the Autodromo Nazionale di Monza, Monza. It was the twelfth race of the 1994 Formula One World Championship.

title: “Penso positivo” by Jovanotti
text: Lorenzo 1994 is the sixth studio album by Italian singer-songwriter Jovanotti, released by Mercury Records on 10 January 1994. The album peaked at number one on the Italian Albums Chart.

title: “All for Love” by Bryan Adams & Sting & Rod Stewart
text: "All for Love" is a song written by Bryan Adams, Robert John "Mutt" Lange, and Michael Kamen for the soundtrack The Three Musketeers: Original Motion Picture Soundtrack. It is performed by Adams, Rod Stewart, and Sting.

title: “The Rhythm of the Night” by Corona
text: "The Rhythm of the Night" is a song by Italian Eurodance group Corona. It was released as their debut single in 1993 in Italy, then elsewhere the following year.

title: “Streets of Philadelphia” by Bruce Springsteen
text: "Streets of Philadelphia" is a song written and performed by American rock musician Bruce Springsteen for the 1993 film Philadelphia, starring Tom Hanks, an early mainstream film dealing with HIV/AIDS. Released as a single by Columbia Records in February 1994, the song was a hit in many countries, topping the singles charts of Austria, Canada, France, Germany, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, and Norway. title: “I'll Remember” by Madonna
text: "I'll Remember" is a song by American singer Madonna for the 1994 film With Honors. It was released by Maverick and Warner Bros.

title: “Eins, Zwei, Polizei” by Mo-Do
text: "Eins, Zwei, Polizei" is a song co-written and recorded by Italian dance musician Mo-Do (a.k.a. Fabio Frittelli) and released in 1994, by label Expanded Music, as the debut single from his first and only album, Was Ist Das?

title: “Sweet Dreams” by La Bouche
text: "Sweet Dreams" is a song recorded by German Eurodance duo La Bouche. It was originally released in April 1994 by RCA Records as the lead single from the duo's debut album of the same name (1995).

title: “The Rhythm Is Magic” by Marie-Claire D'Ubaldo
text: "The Rhythm Is Magic" is a song by Argentine London-based singer-songwriter Marie-Claire D'Ubaldo, released in 1994 by Polydor Records as the first single from the singer's second album, Alma De Barro/Marie-Claire D'Ubaldo. The song is written by D'Ubaldo with Frank Musker and Richard Darbyshire, who also produced it with Phil Chapman.

title: “7 Seconds” by Youssou N'Dour & Neneh Cherry
text: "7 Seconds" is a song performed by Senegalese singer-songwriter Youssou N'Dour and Swedish singer-songwriter Neneh Cherry. The pair also wrote the lyrics, with music composed by producers Cameron McVey and Jonathan Sharp (Jonny Dollar).

title: “Saturday Night” by Whigfield
text: "Saturday Night" is a song by Italian Eurodance project Whigfield, fronted by Danish-born Sannie Charlotte Carlson. It was first released in 1992 in Italy, followed by a Spanish release in 1993.

title: “Short Dick Man” by 20 Fingers
text: "Short Dick Man" is a song by American hip house group 20 Fingers featuring rapper Gillette. It was released in August 1994 on Zoo Entertainment and SOS Records as their debut single from their album, On the Attack and More (1994).

title: “It's a Rainy Day” by Ice MC
text: "It's a Rainy Day" is a song by British, Italy based Eurodance artist Ice MC, released in August 1994 by Italian label Dance World Attack as the third single from his third album, Ice'n'Green, on which it appears in two versions, and his eleventh single overall.
